source.title: Toward a universal law of generalization for psychological science.

confidence_rationale: Canonical, heavily replicated foundational result (Science, 1987; re-confirmed for naturalistic stimuli as recently as 2023) that a stimulus set induces a metric PSYCHOLOGICAL space in which generalization decays as an invariant (near-exponential) function of distance. This is direct, high-source-quality evidence for ARC-087's core premise -- perception contributes a structured GEOMETRY of difference, not raw signal -- and for Q-065's learned-metric arm (the metric is recoverable from similarity/generalization statistics). Confidence held below source_quality because the mapping is one level of abstraction removed: Shepard's space is a general psychological-similarity space, not specifically a per-sense perceptual adaptor manifold.
failure_signatures: The law is a metric-recovery and generalization result, not a constructive account of HOW a sensory adaptor builds the metric -- it constrains the target geometry but does not specify the transform (so it under-determines ARC-087's adaptor stage).

Shepard's two admissible metrics (Euclidean for integral dimensions, city-block for separable) assume a locally additive metric structure; later colour-geometry work (Bujack 2022) shows perceptual spaces can violate additivity at large differences, bounding the universality claim.

mapping.source_claim_statement: For any stimulus set one can construct a metric psychological space such that the probability a learned response generalizes from one stimulus to another is an invariant, monotonically decreasing (approximately exponential) function of their distance in that space; this follows from universal principles of natural kinds and probabilistic geometry plausibly internalized by evolution.
mapping.ree_translation: A sensory modality does not deliver raw values to the world model; it delivers a SHAPED metric over possible differences (ARC-087's perceptual manifold). Shepard supplies the abstract justification for that metric existing and being recoverable from similarity/generalization structure -- which is exactly Q-065's 'learned from the statistics of perceptual similarity' arm. The exponential generalization gradient is the kind of structured, non-trivial geometry the adaptor must produce.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Shepard characterizes a general psychological-similarity space, not a sense-specific perceptual adaptor. It tells us the adaptor's OUTPUT is a metric space with lawful generalization, but says nothing about per-sense adaptor DEPTH (MECH-372) and does not settle the learned-vs-defined fork (Q-065 part 1) -- the same exponential law is compatible with both a learned metric and an evolutionarily internalized structural prior.
mapping.source_context: Human and animal generalization data synthesized into a formal theory; psychophysics + probabilistic-geometry derivation.

confidence_components.notes: source_quality very high (canonical, replicated, cross-species). mapping_fidelity moderate -- abstract similarity space, not an adaptor mechanism. transfer_risk low because the law is explicitly claimed universal across sentient organisms.
